function.name: ask_human
function.description: Ask the user questions only for an irreversible decision, subjective preference/product intent, or a fact unavailable from the conversation, files, and tools. First inspect context, use a quick read/grep when useful, and take a sensible reversible default when the user can correct the result. Do not ask for something you can decide. Supports free text or choices; `questions[]` asks 2-8 questions as one form. blocking=true (default) means pause and ask: the turn waits for the answer, so use it only when nothing useful can proceed without it. blocking=false shows the question and returns at once: state in the question which default you apply meanwhile and keep working on what does not depend on the answer; the reply arrives later as a normal user message quoting the question. A lead (project Coordinator or Global Router) withdraws its own open question that the conversation has since settled with `withdraw: {guidance_id, reason}` and nothing else: the card is marked withdrawn and stops counting as an open owner question; it stays answerable, and an owner answer that comes anyway still arrives and overrides the withdrawal.

With project: a file of that project, relative to its root or absolute inside it (no symlinks). With worker: a file of that Worker's checkout, relative to its root (no symlinks).

function.name: consider_project_message
function.description: Delivered messages are accepted on delivery; call this only to record a rejected, deferred or conflict decision (or to change one) and explain why. Reads the immutable original message; this action never starts another worker, grants tools, or proves delivery. accepted is a stated commitment only and does not authorize new external side effects. Use the revision the delivered message shows (or get_project_messages) as expected_revision; a conflict requires reading current authority, not overwriting another decision. No automatic ACK-of-ACK notification is generated.

instruction_id.description: An active standing instruction of the owner that covers this. Give it with exactly one of event_id or source_turn_id naming what triggered it; instruction_id alone is refused before anything runs.

event_id.description: With instruction_id: the event that triggered it, instead of source_turn_id. Never without instruction_id.

under_delegation.description: true: no owner message asks for this; act on your own judgment under the owner's full delegation to every lead (owner decision 2026-11-18). Give it alone, never with another trigger; reason says why.

function.name: create_memory
function.description: Save a verified reusable lesson: project convention, reproduced failure/root cause/fix, or documented tool/API quirk. Never store secrets (refused), personal details about anyone, identity/preferences (use My Context), one-off requests, chat summaries, speculation, reasoning, or transcripts. When existing lessons match, the first call writes nothing and shows them; call again with repeat_of.

description.description: Write first: dense sentence front-loading searchable symptom, symbol/file, and verified fix/rule; drives search and prefetch.

trigger.description: The situation in which this lesson applies, as it looks before the fix is known: the kind of request or work, files/commands/tools involved, and the symptom or exact error text. Not the cause or fix.

body.description: Concise Markdown: context, reusable rule/fix, and verification evidence; no chat/reasoning recap.

scope.description: global applies across projects; project only to the current project. Default: project

repeat_of.description: Your decision after the matching lessons were shown: "new" records a new lesson; a shown lesson's id records that this mistake happened again despite it: your complete text becomes its new version and its repeat count rises.

items.description: One concrete, checkable requirement of the result.

acceptance.description: Concrete, checkable requirements the result must meet, one per item (for example "pytest tests/x passes"). The Worker sees them numbered from 1 and reports evidence for each; review_project_work judges each by its number. With rework_of, omit it to keep the reworked assignment's checks; a list replaces them.

attachments.description: Files to send with it, exactly as send_project_message's attachments describes (the one full definition).

review.description: Independent review loop for this Worker's result (docs/PROJECT_COORDINATION.md, "Review loops"). When the Worker finishes, each reviewer is started as its own Worker with no author context; findings of a failed audit go back to this Worker as a follow_up and fresh reviewers re-audit, until every reviewer passes or an impasse is reported. Poll the returned review_loop_id.

role.description: correctness: recompute numbers, tables and figures from sources (data audit); overclaim: claims versus evidence; references: citations and cross-references; custom: the audit named in focus.

focus.description: Extra audit instructions for this reviewer; required for custom.

function.name: delete_memory
function.description: Delete an obsolete, incorrect, or duplicate memory.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Replace text in files read/written in an earlier round. Each edit finds `anchor`, copied exactly from the file, and replaces it with `content`; empty content deletes. The anchor must match once; replace_all replaces every match. To add text, keep neighbouring text in both: after A: `{"anchor":"A","content":"A\nB"}`; before A: `{"anchor":"A","content":"B\nA"}`. Append at end-of-file with write_file(append=true). Name the file once in `path`; set an edit's `path` only for another file. Later edits see earlier changes. Atomic preflight defaults true: any failure writes nothing. With atomic=false, one failure neither rolls back nor stops the others. I/O failures may leave partial writes.

description.description: Optional pre-edit caption (max 120 chars). Omit it to use the file-path label.

path.description: File this batch edits. Write it once here for a single-file batch instead of repeating it on every edit; an edit's own `path` overrides it.
File for this edit, when it differs from the batch `path`. Never inherited from the previous edit; omit it rather than sending an empty string.

content.description: Complete new text, including kept anchor text and line breaks; empty deletes.

atomic.description: Preflight all edits before writing. False permits partial application.

function.name: edit_slides
function.description: Edit ONE or SEVERAL pages of a deck created by produce_slides, in plain language — e.g. '第 3 页标题改成…', 'make page 2 dark', '给第 5 页加一个柱状图'. Each page is re-authored from its CURRENT layout (everything else stays), re-validated, re-rendered and the PPTX is re-exported once at the end. Use this for content rewrites / layout restructuring; for simple field-level changes (改文字/字号/颜色/图片) prefer patch_slides (deterministic, no LLM, seconds). Pass `page` for one page or `pages` for a batch (≤8) sharing one instruction.

page.description: 1-based page number to edit (single-page form; mutually exclusive with pages).

pages.description: 1-based page numbers for a batch edit with the same instruction (≤8 pages).

instruction.description: What to change on that page, in the user's words.

function.name: edit_video
function.description: Edit ONE scene of a video created by produce_video, in plain language — e.g. '把第 2 个镜头的标题改成…', 'make scene 3 slower and darker', '给第 4 镜换成柱状图表达'. Two modes: 'rewrite' (default) has the scene author rewrite that scene's composition from its CURRENT frame (everything else stays; the better of old/new wins), then only that scene is re-rendered and the final video re-assembled in place. 'set_narration' replaces the scene's spoken narration text deterministically (new TTS must FIT the scene's existing duration — shorten the text when it overflows); the frame is untouched and only the audio/subtitles rebuild. Returns immediately with an edit task_id. Use this for follow-up edits instead of regenerating the whole film. Scene numbers are 1-based (scene-001 … scene-NNN also accepted).

scene.description: Scene to edit: 1-based number ('2') or scene id ('scene-002').

instruction.description: rewrite: what to change in that scene, in the user's words. set_narration: the NEW narration text for the scene. set_subtitle_style: a short note (may be a placeholder like '字幕样式'). swap_asset: the QUERY describing the replacement asset.

op.description: Edit mode (default 'rewrite'). set_subtitle_style is JOB-LEVEL (scene may be omitted) and needs `style`.

style.description: set_subtitle_style: subtitle overrides — font_scale (0.6..1.8), font_px (10..200), margin_v (px from bottom), outline (0..12), font_name.

model.description: Optional model id locking the scene author for this edit (rewrite only).

asset_kind.description: swap_asset: fetch stock media (default), AI-generate a still, or 't2v' — a text-to-video CLIP (video targets only, needs TOFU_T2V_* configured).

target.description: swap_asset: the scene's current media path to replace (required only when the scene references several media files).

calls.description: Tool calls. Use a task-executable exact name and arguments that match its schema; search_tools is optional.

function.name: fetch_url
function.description: Read remote HTTP(S) HTML/PDF/text; follow relevant Page Links. Local paths/file://: read_files. Text supports artifact paging; binaries return server-staging paths. If HTTP lacks login, the selected browser streams bytes to staging, never browser Downloads. Use an authorized filesystem tool to copy/move and verify receipt. Concurrent batch urls:[{url}]: url ignored; extract: single mode. extract returns quote-backed findings and unresolved requests from bounded windows; gaps do not prove absence. Raw source stays artifact-readable; failure returns raw.

url.description: Single HTTP(S) URL; omit with urls.

urls.description: Concurrent batch of {url} objects; url ignored.

function.name: find_files
function.description:
Find files by name pattern (glob) in the project. Useful for discovering test files, configs, etc.

**Prefer this over ``run_command find``** — find_files is served from a persistent project file index (near-instant even on huge or network-mounted trees), supports ``max_results``, includes hidden files, and auto-filters ignored paths (node_modules, .venv, .gitignore matches, etc.) unless ``path`` points inside one.

For MULTIPLE searches, provide a 'searches' array — each entry has the same fields as the top-level parameters. Batch mode cuts round trips.

path.description: Relative path to search in (optional)

max_results.description: Maximum number of files to return. Default 100. Use a small value (5-20) when you only need a quick sample.

searches.description: Array of find operations. All entries execute with the same fields as the top-level parameters. Faster than separate find_files calls.

path.description: Relative path to search in (optional)

function.name: generate_image
function.description: Create/draw/design an image, or edit one supplied by the user or produced earlier. For edits, pass the exact source_image reference and describe only the desired changes; a capable edit model preserves unmentioned content. Success returns a project path or /api/images/... reference—reuse it for later edits instead of regenerating. Use a detailed English prompt; aspect_ratio and resolution are optional.

prompt.description: Detailed English scene (style, composition, colors, lighting) or edit instruction describing only desired changes.

source_image.description: Existing image URL/path to edit, including local /api/images/... or a remote URL. Use the exact result reference; omit to generate a new image.

output_path.description: Optional project-relative destination; missing directories are created. If omitted or no project is active, saves to server uploads. Multi-root: rootname:subdir targets that root; bare relative uses primary. The prefix is routing, not a literal filename.

svg.description: Also use vtracer with background removal to save a same-name .svg beside the PNG; useful for scalable logos, icons, and illustrations. Default false.

function.name: get_agent_messages
function.description: Read durable message evidence for exactly one target without starting work. Two target forms exist; choose one and do not mix their fields. Form A, exact run: pass agent_id AND swarm_run_id, plus optional message_id, to inspect input receipts in a temporary spawn_agents run, including a worker's own inbox. Example: {"agent_id":"child","swarm_run_id":"launch"}. Form B, stable colleague: pass retained_agent_id AND the original idempotency_key, plus optional scope, to inspect that message's pinned assignment and outcome; stable-agent reads remain root-only. Read on demand after uncertainty; input_confirmed does not prove acceptance or completion. Old messages never steer or activate replacement runs.

idempotency_key.description: Required for a stable-agent receipt lookup.

function.name: get_agent_result
function.description:
Fetch the FULL final answer of one or more completed sub-agents again. Completion updates already carry the full result — use this to re-read an earlier result after it aged out of your context.

Results are durable per run: pass `swarm_run_id` (from the spawn_agents handle or a `<swarm-update>`) to read a run of this conversation that has ended, was evicted after inactivity, or was replaced by a later wave. Without it, ids resolve in the current swarm.

For MULTIPLE agents in one call, provide an `agent_ids` array — all results come back together in a single `results` list. This is much better than issuing several separate get_agent_result calls: prefer ONE batched call when you want the full bodies of the agents a `spawn_agents` wave produced.

For agents that are still running, the entry reports a running-status notice; for unknown ids it reports an error — neither aborts the rest of the batch.

swarm_run_id.description: Exact run handle: `swarm_run_id` of the spawn_agents handle or `<swarm-run-id>` of a `<swarm-update>`. Needed for an ended, evicted or earlier wave; omit for the current swarm.

agent_id.description: A single agent id from a `<swarm-update>` payload or the spawn_agents handle. Single-fetch mode; omit when using `agent_ids`.

agent_ids.description: Array of agent ids to fetch in ONE call (batch mode). All results are returned together in the `results` field. Use INSTEAD of `agent_id` when you need several agents' full bodies — do NOT issue N separate get_agent_result calls.

function.name: get_conversation
function.description:
Retrieve a conversation by ID when the user explicitly requests past-conversation information. A bound project Coordinator may also inspect same-owner, same-project worker evidence needed to delegate, review or follow the current authorized request. Otherwise do not browse history proactively. Use an ID from list_conversations or the current assignment/result evidence.

The current conversation's own ID needs no user request: it returns this conversation's durable transcript, including Turns that may be outside your current working view (for example after compaction). Page to those older Turns with before=N.

To read a specific Turn (for example a list_conversations match), pass turn_id: the page around that Turn, with older/newer before=N hints in the header.

`raw` defaults to true: a structured, unsummarized DB record with row metadata/settings and every field of each delivered message, including full tool rounds. Set `raw=false` only for a readable transcript; it drops per-message metadata and condenses tool rounds.

Long histories return a parseable head+tail window of whole messages. Check `DELIVERED N of M`; use its positive `before=N` hint for older pages. `limit` widens the window but may clamp fields, which the header reports.

conversation_id.description: Conversation ID, usually from list_conversations; the current conversation's own ID reads its durable transcript.

include_tool_details.description: For raw=false only, include full tool arguments/results (default true); false shortens them. Raw mode always includes them.

raw.description: Default true: structured raw record with all fields of each delivered message. False returns readable prose that drops message metadata and condenses tool rounds.

limit.description: Recent-message count (min 1). Omit for a budget-fit whole-message window; too large may clamp fields, reported in the header.

before.description: Exclusive 1-based end cursor (min 1) for an older page. Omit for latest; use the header's positive before=N hint. Never pass 0.

turn_id.description: Read the page containing this main-transcript Turn, e.g. a Turn ID named by a list_conversations match. Exclusive with before.

lane_id.description: Turn laneId to list; default main.

before_ordinal.description: Exact window.next_before_ordinal from the previous result.

function.name: get_project_messages
function.description: Read a bounded incoming or outgoing mailbox for this same-project conversation. Does not read private transcripts or start work. State input_confirmed is distinct from an explicit recipient consideration decision, and accepted is not proof of execution or delivery. Do not busy-poll. A conversation_id is required for outgoing; it identifies the recipient mailbox, which may be another project's lead you messaged.

limit.description: Page size for scope=request. Project history always reads a bounded 32-row storage page.

scope.description: request lists this original human input; project reads current Coordinator history, up to 32 rows per page. after_id is the returned next_cursor.

after_id.description: The next_cursor of the previous page (get_project_workers convention).

pattern.description: Short literal substring preferred; Rust/ripgrep regex is supported.

path.description: One relative path; omit for project root.

context_lines.description: Lines before/after each match. Default 0, max 10; use 3-5 to avoid a follow-up read.

max_results.description: Matching-line cap, default 50; use 5-20 for samples/existence checks.

from_line.description: Only report matches on lines ≥ N (per-file floor for paging).

count_only.description: Return the full matching-line count only; `max_results` is ignored in count_only mode.

searches.description: Batch operations; all entries execute. Faster than separate calls.

path.description: Relative path to search in (optional)

function.name: inspect_image
function.description: Read fine detail by transforming the ORIGINAL image at source resolution before model downscaling. Read the whole image once, then inspect ONE crop/zoom region per call; many returned images are downscaled together. Use grid=true first for 0–1 coordinates, then crop. READ-ONLY; never changes the source.

path.description: Local path using read_files rules (png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp), or a chat upload's shown /api/images/<file> reference. Do not invent a path such as /dev/null.

crop.description: Keep [x0,y0,x1,y1]. Each 0–1 value is its axis fraction; >1 is pixels, and units may mix. Coordinates follow the visible frame after EXIF orientation then rotate. [.5,0,1,.5] is the top-right quadrant. Crop wins over zoom; omit for the whole frame. Prefer grid fractions.

zoom.description: Centre zoom >1; 2 keeps the middle quarter. Used only when crop is omitted.

rotate.description: Clockwise degrees after EXIF orientation; default 0.

grid.description: Overlay labelled 0–1 coordinates for a later crop; default false.

function.name: inspect_video
function.description: Watch a local video or hear an audio file: probe facts, timestamped key frames as images (video) and, when speech-to-text is available, a transcript. Pass start/end seconds to inspect one section densely. Read-only.

path.description: Project-relative or absolute path (e.g. a data/fetched/ file from fetch_url or browser_download_url_to_server), or an att_media_<id> chat video reference.

function.name: integration_checkpoint
function.description: Capture the current isolated writer workspace as a checkpoint. The runtime binds this call to this execution's automatic work ID.

function.name: integration_submit
function.description: Save a checkpoint of this execution. Automatic task changes are merged into the current canonical workspace at successful completion, independently of commits and release gates. Explicit candidate submissions retain their review/checker policy.

summary.description: What changed and how it was verified.

function.name: kill
function.description: Stop background work by handle: a bg_* background command (its process tree receives SIGTERM then SIGKILL) or a RUNNING swarm sub-agent. There is no timeout auto-kill — this is how background work is stopped. Tasks in other conversations cannot be killed from here; use that conversation's Stop control. Call poll with no arguments first if unsure what is running.

id.description: Handle to stop: a bg_* command id or a swarm agent id. Legacy alias command_id is accepted.

function.name: list_agents
function.description: List reusable team agents in the current project or conversation. Pass agent_id to inspect one agent and a bounded view of its remembered recent dialogue. This is read-only; use manage_agents to create, assign, reset, archive, restore, or delete.

scope.description: Omit to use the current default scope.

function.name: list_conversations
function.description: Search other conversations when the user explicitly asks for past-conversation information. A bound project Coordinator may also inspect same-owner, same-project worker evidence needed to delegate, review or follow the current authorized request. Otherwise do not browse history proactively. Project mode scopes to siblings; scope=all requires an explicit user request beyond that project. The current conversation is never listed; the result names its ID for get_conversation. A keyword match in message text names the matching Turn ID and a snippet (also for the current conversation); read that page with get_conversation(conversation_id, turn_id).

after_id.description: The next_cursor of the previous page.

include_resources.description: Also return the registry's full text on the first page; a long one arrives in pages readable with read_tool_artifact.

function.name: load_skill
function.description: Load the whole installed skill guide and its resource manifest. An empty manifest means instruction-only: do not invent skill:// paths. Call it before using a matching workflow. A skill is guidance only and grants no permissions.

function.name: local_serve_deploy
function.description: Deploy a local model as a managed server: install the selected engine into an isolated venv (bounded disk budget), launch it on 127.0.0.1 in the managed port band, wait for readiness (retrying with degraded parameters on OOM), and register the endpoint as a selectable model provider. REQUIRES human approval. Returns immediately after the plan is approved — the deployment proceeds in the background; poll local_serve_status with the returned instance_id until status is 'running' or 'failed'. Always run local_serve_prepare first and only call this after the user agrees to the plan.

function.name: local_serve_list
function.description: List every known managed local deployment with its engine, model path, status, endpoint, and last error. Read-only.

function.name: local_serve_prepare
function.description: Inspect a local model path (HuggingFace directory or .gguf file), probe this machine's GPU/RAM/disk, and return the recommended engine with exact launch parameters, resource tier, and the OOM degradation ladder. Read-only — run this FIRST and relay the plan to the user before any deployment. Fails with a structured error when the path is missing or not a recognised model (never guess: ask the user for the real path).

model_path.description: Absolute path to the model on THIS machine: a directory containing config.json (HF/transformers layout) or a single .gguf file.

engine.description: Optional engine override. Omit to let the planner pick the most stable engine for the detected model and hardware.

function.name: local_serve_recommend
function.description: Probe this machine's GPU/RAM/disk and rank a curated catalog of open-weight models (Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1-Distill, Llama, Gemma…) against it: each candidate comes with the best variant (BF16 for vLLM / Q4_K_M GGUF for llama.cpp), the fit tier (comfortable/tight/extreme/cpu), and the exact download command. When the hardware cannot comfortably run a capable model, the response includes a cheap cloud API alternative (DeepSeek V4 Flash) instead — offer it honestly rather than pushing a hopeless local install. Read-only. Use this FIRST whenever the user wants a local model but has not picked one yet; once they choose, guide the download, then local_serve_prepare + local_serve_deploy.

purpose.description: Optional use-case filter. Omit for a general ranking across all categories.

function.name: local_serve_remove
function.description: Remove a managed deployment entirely: stop the server, unregister its provider (the model disappears from the model picker), and delete the ledger row. REQUIRES human approval. The engine venv and the user's model files are NOT deleted.

function.name: local_serve_status
function.description: Report one managed deployment: phase (planned/installing/starting/running/stopped/failed), live pid + /models probe, last error, and a log tail. Use it to poll after local_serve_deploy (deployments can take minutes — model load and first-run engine downloads are slow) and to diagnose a failed start. On 'failed' the response carries a structured diagnosis {kind, summary, suggestions, retryable} — relay the summary and suggestions, then act: retryable=true means re-calling local_serve_deploy is worthwhile (possibly after the user frees VRAM/disk); retryable=false means the model, engine, or driver must change first — offer to pick a smaller model via local_serve_recommend or the cloud alternative.

function.name: local_serve_stop
function.description: Stop a running managed deployment (SIGTERM to the server process group). The deployment stays registered as stopped and can be started again with local_serve_deploy. Stopping frees GPU/RAM but any conversation using the model loses it.

function.name: manage_agents
function.description: Manage reusable team agents. A retained agent remembers prior assignments across turns and restarts while using no worker when idle. Use spawn_agents for one-off independent work. Create once, then assign later objectives by agent_id; the assignment runs as an ordinary async Swarm child and returns via <swarm-update>. Assign requires an idle identity; a busy agent rejects another assignment. Use send_agent_message with retained_agent_id to message this colleague: busy adds input to the owned current assignment; idle starts the next turn with saved dialogue. Cancelled colleagues require intent=resume. For steering only, send the exact agent_id plus swarm_run_id; it never starts replacement work. Use get_agent_messages with the original target and idempotency_key to reconcile uncertainty. Do not treat assign as live steering. Scope defaults to the current project, or conversation when no project is attached. Current tool permissions apply on every run. Use list_agents to inspect a bounded memory view. Reset clears working memory; archive pauses assignments; delete removes the retained record. Promote copies a completed temporary Swarm child in this conversation into a new retained identity.

scope.description: Omit to use the current default scope.

agent_id.description: Required except for create and list.

source_agent_id.description: Completed Swarm child ID for promote.

tools.description: Optional narrow-only tool allowlist for this run.

abandon.description: For reset of a busy agent: fence its late memory result.

function.name: merge_memories
function.description: Consolidate 2–32 overlapping memories, then delete originals. Use when one replacement is clearer; deletion failures are reported.

description.description: Write first: dense sentence front-loading merged search triggers and the verified rule.

trigger.description: The situation in which this lesson applies, as it looks before the fix is known: the kind of request or work, files/commands/tools involved, and the symptom or exact error text. Not the cause or fix.

tags.description: Merged tags; omit to union source tags.

function.name: motion_video_check
function.description: Run the HyperFrames static gates (lint + headless-Chrome validate + layout inspect) on one scene or whole-film project dir. MANDATORY before rendering. If continuity.json is present, also sample each declared handoff in a real browser: persistent DOM identity, visibility, geometry and reverse-seek pixel repeatability. Returns boundary contact-sheet paths for visual review. On failure returns categorized errors with upstream fix hints — repair the composition in place and re-check (max 2 repair rounds).

function.name: motion_video_concat
function.description: Assemble final.mp4 from ordered scene MP4s. Uniform specs concat losslessly (-c copy); mismatched scenes are re-encode-normalized to the first scene's spec. Optional transitions execute real FFmpeg xfade edits. For every overlap, the outgoing scene MUST already include an equal visual tail handle; then the final program duration stays aligned with narration/SRT. Output is atomic and post-verified.

transitions.description: Optional ordered N-1 boundary plan. Zero duration is a hard cut; non-zero boundaries consume an equal outgoing visual handle from the previous clip.

function.name: motion_video_env_check
function.description: Check (and optionally bootstrap) the motion-video render environment: Node>=22, the HyperFrames CLI (auto-installed pinned version when missing), ffmpeg, ffprobe (optional), and a headless Chrome. Call this first when a motion_video_* tool reports env_missing, or before your first render on a fresh deployment. Before authoring your first scene, read the vendored guides lib/motion_video/guide/WORKFLOW.md and COMPOSITION_CONTRACT.md (absolute paths under the tofu install) and start each scene from lib/motion_video/guide/skeleton.html. For one-take films with objects/camera carried between beats, read CONTINUOUS_FILM.md and start from guide/continuous/ (one index.html + continuity.json, no clip concat).

install.description: When true (default), auto-install the pinned HyperFrames CLI into the tofu data dir if it is missing. First install downloads npm packages and can take a minute.

function.name: motion_video_mux
function.description: Final audio step. With audio_plan_path, stage and hash licensed local BGM/SFX, resolve cues against scenes/beat time, duck BGM under narration, mix to -14 LUFS, and emit audio_plan.json + audio_attribution.txt. Without a plan, mux the single narration track using the legacy loudnorm path. Runtime audio downloads are forbidden. Post-verified: audio present and program duration preserved.

audio.description: Optional narration track. Required when no audio plan is provided; optional for BGM/SFX-only delivery.

loudnorm.description: Apply EBU R128 loudness normalization (default true).

audio_plan_path.description: Optional motion-audio-v1 JSON, relative to the project or absolute. Its asset paths resolve beside the plan.

scenes_path.description: scenes.json carrying motion-timeline-v1 fields; required for scene-relative SFX cues.

function.name: motion_video_narrate
function.description: P2 音画合成 step 1: synthesize per-scene TTS narration WAVs from a storyboard scenes.json. Returns an alignment manifest — in the default 'loose' mode each scene's target_duration = max(srt, audio + tail_pad); when target_duration exceeds the SRT duration you MUST update that scene's data-duration before rendering. Degrades gracefully (ok=false, degraded=true) when no TTS slot is configured — deliver the silent video.

alignment.description: 'loose' (default): scene duration follows the audio. 'strict': SRT span is fixed; over-long narration is reported as overflow for you to shorten the text.

function.name: motion_video_probe
function.description: Probe a media file (ffprobe, ffmpeg fallback): codec, resolution, fps, duration, audio-track presence. Use after every render and after concat to verify specs.

path.description: Media file path (project-relative or absolute).

function.name: motion_video_render
function.description: Render one scene OR one continuous whole-film composition to MP4 via HyperFrames. Opted-in continuity.json handoffs must pass browser checks; render refuses failed/unavailable evidence. No concat is needed for a continuous film. Cost is ~3.5x realtime on this host (a 10s scene ≈ 35s). Use quality 'draft' while iterating, 'standard' for delivery, 'high' for final takes. After rendering, verify with motion_video_probe (resolution/fps/duration/silence).

output.description: Output MP4 path (project-relative or absolute, e.g. .tofu/motion_video/<slug>/scenes/scene-001/scene-001.mp4).

timeout.description: Wall-clock seconds before the render is killed (default 1800; 0 = no limit).

function.name: motion_video_storyboard_check
function.description: Zero-LLM gate: validate a scenes.json storyboard against its SRT transcript — required fields, monotonic contiguity, FULL coverage of the SRT span, and scene-duration sum equal to the span within ±0.1s. MANDATORY before rendering any scene. Returns a list of human-readable errors (empty = pass).

srt_path.description: Path to the SRT transcript (project-relative or absolute).

scenes_path.description: Path to scenes.json — a list of {id, start, end, text, visual?} with float seconds.

action.description: list: the reversible settings keys and their current values; get: one key; set: write one key through the Settings save backend; channel: read (enabled omitted) or toggle a messaging channel (enabled given), reporting preconditions first.

path.description: The dotted settings key for get/set: model_defaults.default_model, model_defaults.fallback_model, hidden_models, hidden_ig_models, search.skip_domains or proxy_bypass_domains; restart_blackouts (the owner's restart blackout windows, a list of {start, end, reason} with ISO 8601 date-times carrying a UTC offset; set needs the owner's own words as trigger, never under_delegation, and [] lifts them; a delegated restart of any lead is refused inside one). Any other key returns needs_owner_action (secret-bearing: mt_provider, feishu, proxy, search.gateway, providers), owner_settings_not_delegated (destructive or external) or owner_settings_unsupported.

value.description: The new value for set. Its type and validation are exactly the Settings backend's; invalid values return the backend's own error.

channel.description: For action=channel: which messaging channel to read or toggle.

enabled.description: For action=channel: the desired enabled state. Omit to read status without changing anything. A relaunch that would push a 大象 login card is never triggered automatically, and a kicked 大象 account reconnects only on the owner's own message; both return needs_owner_action.

reason.description: Why you act for the owner, naming what they asked for; it is kept in the owner's audit log.

source_turn_id.description: Without instruction_id: the Turn ID of the owner's own message in your current request that asks for this. With instruction_id: the Turn that carried the triggering event, instead of event_id.

source_steer_id.description: The steer_id of an owner message sent while you were replying that asks for this. Never combined with source_turn_id, instruction_id or event_id.

instruction_id.description: An active standing instruction of the owner that covers this. Give it with exactly one of event_id or source_turn_id naming what triggered it; instruction_id alone is refused before anything runs.

event_id.description: With instruction_id: the event that triggered it, instead of source_turn_id. Never without instruction_id.

under_delegation.description: true: no owner message asks for this; act on your own judgment under the owner's full delegation to every lead (owner decision 2026-11-18). Give it alone, never with another trigger; reason says why.

idempotency_key.description: One setting change per key: a retry with the same key returns the recorded change and never applies it twice.

function.name: paper_build
function.description: Compile this conversation's LaTeX paper project through the bounded build service and read the verified result: status, engine, and structured diagnostics with file/line positions. ALWAYS call this after creating or editing .tex/.bib/.sty/.cls files: if the build failed, fix every error at its reported file:line and compile again before finishing — never leave the project in a state that does not compile. action='diagnostics' reports the most recent build without recompiling (cheap check). The document defaults to the conversation's selected paper document; pass `path` to target a specific main .tex file instead.

action.description: 'compile' (default) runs a fresh build and waits for the verified receipt; 'diagnostics' only reports the latest build for the resolved document.

path.description: Optional main .tex file or source directory, relative to the project root. Defaults to the selected paper document.

engine.description: TeX engine override; 'auto' detects from the preamble (default).

function.name: paper_check
function.description: Submission-readiness gate for the LaTeX paper: source-level academic QA rules (unreferenced figures, hard-coded numbers, caption style, heading structure, missing graphics files, undefined refs/citations) plus PDF-level checks on the latest build (fonts embedded — a hard IEEE/ACM requirement, image DPI, page count). Run before declaring the paper finished; fix all errors, then re-verify with paper_build.

path.description: Optional main .tex file or source directory, relative to the project root. Defaults to the selected paper document.

scope.description: 'all' (default) runs source checks and, when a successful build is retained, PDF checks; 'source' or 'pdf' restrict to one family.

function.name: paper_citation_audit
function.description: Audit local .bib entries / \cite keys and verify a bounded batch against OpenAlex. Follow next_cursor to cover the bibliography; retry_cursor retries unverified rows in that batch. Keep the same path. Source edits invalidate cursors. Skipped entries remain unverified; combine all page results with the same source_digest before judging full-document coverage. A last page does not certify earlier pages. Flags probable-hallucinated entries (not found), metadata mismatches (title/year/author), RETRACTED papers, duplicate keys, undefined citations and unused entries. Run before submission or after bulk citation edits.

path.description: Optional main .tex file to select the paper document. Defaults to the conversation's selected paper document.

cursor.description: Continuation from next_cursor, or retry_cursor to recheck a batch with skipped entries. Omit to start a new audit.

function.name: paper_cite_insert
function.description: Fetch the work's real BibTeX (Crossref/OpenAlex), append it to the project's .bib (deduplicated), and insert \cite{key} at the anchor in a .tex file. anchor = a short unique search string in the file; the \cite is inserted right after the anchor text. Omit anchor to only add the .bib entry.

doi.description: DOI of the work to cite, e.g. 10.1038/nature14539 (from paper_cite_search). Exactly one of doi/openalex_id/arxiv is required.

openalex_id.description: OpenAlex work ID, e.g. W2741809807 or https://openalex.org/W2741809807.

key.description: BibTeX cite key override (1-64 chars of A-Za-z0-9:_./-). Defaults to a proposed firstauthorYearTitleword key.

cite_file.description: .bib file, relative to the project root, to append the entry to. Defaults to the first existing .bib next to the paper; refs.bib is created if none exists.

tex_file.description: .tex file, relative to the project root, for the anchor insertion. Defaults to the paper's main file.

anchor.description: Short UNIQUE search string in tex_file (4-300 chars, must occur exactly once). \cite{key} is inserted right after it. Omit to only add the .bib entry.

anchor_position.description: Insert the \cite after (default) or before the anchor text.

path.description: Optional main .tex file to select the paper document, as in paper_build. Defaults to the selected document.

function.name: paper_cite_search
function.description: Search REAL academic literature (OpenAlex, 250M works) to cite. Returns verified candidate works with DOIs, venue, year, citation counts and retraction flags. ALWAYS search before inserting a citation — never invent references.

query.description: Free-text search: title keywords, author names, topic, or a combination, e.g. 'attention is all you need' or 'vaswani transformer'.

function.name: paper_import_arxiv
function.description: Import an arXiv paper's TeX SOURCE into this conversation's project root as a compilable project: downloads the bounded e-print archive, extracts it atomically into a fresh arxiv-<id>/ directory (never overwrites existing files), discovers the main document and selects it for the paper preview. Use this when the user wants to read, reuse, or build on an arXiv paper's LaTeX — then edit sources and verify with paper_build. Requires a local project folder attached to the conversation.

arxiv.description: arXiv ID or URL, e.g. 2301.12345 or https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.12345

function.name: paper_layout
function.description: Report the page budget of the conversation's LaTeX paper from the latest verified build: total page count, where each section starts (file:line → PDF page), and how full the last page is. Use this to answer 'how many pages is it now' and to plan page-limit work — e.g. when asked to compress to N pages, read which sections span the most pages, shorten those, then re-verify with paper_build. Never edits anything; reads the latest retained build.

path.description: Optional main .tex file, relative to the project root. Defaults to the selected paper document.

function.name: paper_propose_edits
function.description: Propose .tex/.bib edits for USER REVIEW instead of applying them directly. Each edit is an exact-anchor search/replace (the same matching rules as apply_diff: include enough context to match once). The user sees every hunk as a diff with accept/reject. Use when the user asks to see changes before they are applied, for risky refactors, or when offering alternative phrasings. The proposal is validated immediately against the current files; hunks that no longer match are marked failed.

path.description: Optional main .tex file or source directory, relative to the project root. Defaults to the selected paper document.

edits.description: Hunks to propose, at most 20. Paths are relative to the paper document's main-file directory.

path.description: Target file, relative to the paper document's main-file directory.

search.description: Exact anchor text to find; must match the current file exactly once.

replace.description: Replacement text (omit or empty to delete the anchor).

description.description: Short human-readable summary of this hunk.

function.name: paper_review
function.description: Assemble a rigorous peer-review dossier for this paper (rubric + the paper's key content + a claims-audit protocol). After calling this, YOU act as an expert reviewer: fill the rubric with 1-10 scores, write strengths/weaknesses/questions, run the claims audit, and end with a prioritized revision plan. Use when the user asks to review/critique the paper or prepare for submission.

path.description: Optional main .tex file or source directory, relative to the project root. Defaults to the selected paper document.

focus.description: Optional review focus requested by the user, e.g. 'soundness of the ablation' or 'related work coverage'.

function.name: paper_scaffold
function.description: Generate a LaTeX paper skeleton proposal (main.tex + per-section stubs) as TEXT for the user to confirm. After confirmation, create the files with write_file. Use when starting a new paper from scratch.

path.description: Optional target directory (relative to the project root) the user has in mind; only echoed back in the proposal, nothing is written.

function.name: patch_slides
function.description: DETERMINISTIC field-level edits to ONE page of a deck created by produce_slides — zero LLM, applies in seconds, fully predictable. PREFER this over edit_slides whenever the user's request maps to a field mutation: 改标题/正文文字 (set_text), 调字号/颜色/加粗 (set_style), 挪位置/改大小 (set_bounds), 换图片 (swap_image), 删元素 (delete), 复制元素 (duplicate). Targets are elementId / componentId shown in the page source; use edit_slides instead when the change needs rewriting copy, restructuring the layout, or editing component internals beyond metric/quote/code scalar fields. Every op is validated and layout-measured; a patch that breaks validation or worsens the page's measured layout is rolled back and reported.

target.description: elementId or componentId on this page.

field.description: set_text on a component: the scalar field (metric: value|label|support|source; quote: text|source; code: code).

props.description: set_style: style fields (fontSize, color, bold, italic, fontFamily, lineHeight, letterSpacing, align, backgroundColor).

bounds.description: set_bounds: [x, y, w, h] in page points.

src.description: swap_image: new image src (deck media path or https).

newId.description: duplicate: optional explicit id for the clone.

function.name: poll
function.description: Check or wait on background work: background shell commands (bg_* handles from run_command), swarm sub-agents from spawn_agents, or tasks running in other conversations. With no id, returns a snapshot of everything currently running. With an id, returns that handle's status — and its full result once finished. Set wait_s to block until completion: the wait returns as soon as the handle finishes, new input arrives for this turn, or the task is stopped, so a long wait costs no extra model requests (capped at 1500 s = 25 minutes; on cap returns the running snapshot — call again to keep waiting). Background command completions are also delivered automatically, so only wait when there is nothing else to do.

id.description: One handle: a bg_* command id, a swarm agent id, or a task id. Legacy aliases command_id / agent_id / task_id are accepted.

wait_s.description: Seconds to block waiting for completion (at most 1500; returns as soon as the handle finishes). Omit for an instant snapshot.

mode.description: With multiple command ids or multiple swarm-agent ids: 'any' (default) returns as soon as one finishes; 'all' waits for every match.

The pipeline researches the topic on the web (every claim grounded in a real source URL), drafts an outline, writes each section, and assembles a cited markdown report published as an artifact. topic.description: The subject to research and report on.

depth.description: brief ≈3 sections, standard ≈5, deep ≈8. Deeper costs more and takes longer.

Novelty and value judgments are provisional and limited to the retrieved evidence. The output is a survey and candidate ideas; research conclusions require reproducible baseline and candidate experiments, independent validation and inspection of originals. Continue the user goal through those stages before claiming empirical gains or publication readiness. Returns immediately with a task_id; the survey runs in the background (several minutes). Use this when the user asks what is worth working on, wants research directions / open problems / a gap analysis in a field — NOT for a written summary of a topic (that is produce_report). Does NOT require an attached project. This is an agent-based tool with an authored workflow: internal models work within fixed stages, with output validation, domain quality checks and durable checkpoints. seed_arxiv_ids.description: Optional arXiv ids to seed the corpus with, e.g. ['2312.00752']. Use when the user names specific papers to start from.

Use `read_files`, `search_files`, `find_files`, `edit_file`, `write_file` for repository data. Form B, stable colleague: pass retained_agent_id (from manage_agents/list_agents); optional scope selects the project or conversation binding, and intent=resume explicitly authorizes a fresh turn after cancellation. A busy colleague receives the message in its current owned assignment; an idle one starts a fresh turn with remembered dialogue and current tools, policy and budget. Supply a unique idempotency_key and reuse unchanged content, kind and intent after uncertainty; use get_agent_messages to reconcile the same stable key or exact run. Agent text grants no human authority; a cross-project message grants no permissions, transcript access or control of the other project's Workers. Preserve the same idempotency_key/content after uncertainty. Use reply_to only for a message exchanged between the same two participants; no transcript access is implied. Messages grant no permissions. manage_agents assign starts an idle identity, never steers a live run.

Roles and exact tool scopes:
  - researcher: Open-ended research questions and information gathering — web searches, doc lookups, comparing libraries, surveying APIs. Choose this role when the answer requires reading multiple web pages or external sources. [tools: web_search, fetch_url, browser_research_page, browser_read_page, browser_list_tabs]
  - coder: Multi-file code investigations or modifications — find usages of X, audit a refactor, write a unit test, run a command and report. Use coder when the task touches code in the project. [tools: read_files, write_file, edit_file, search_files, find_files, run_command, poll, kill]
  - analyst: Quantitative analysis of data already on disk — log parsing, metric extraction, finding patterns in CSV / JSON / structured output. Choose this when the answer is numbers / tables. [tools: read_files, search_files, run_command, poll, kill]
  - browser: Tasks that require interacting with already-open browser tabs — click buttons, fill forms, scrape JS-rendered pages, take screenshots, or download a visible page asset into server staging. Use this when web_search / fetch_url cannot reach the content because it needs interaction.   - reviewer: Get a fresh, independent read on code or design — security review, bug hunting, code-style audit. Choose this for "second opinion" tasks where you want eyes that have not seen your analysis. Outputs a concrete punch list. [tools: read_files, search_files, find_files, run_command, poll, kill]

  - general: Mixed / unclear tasks where no single specialist role fits — a sub-task that needs a couple of different tool families together. Default fallback when in doubt. Choose this for 2+ independent branches or context isolation; keep trivial or sequential work local. Hand a worker exact tools through its `tools` allowlist instead of loading them yourself. If the task needs a tool not listed by any specialist, use 'general'. Sub-agents cannot spawn or ask the user; provide self-contained objectives. When a worker reports a missing tool, Re-spawn the same task with general or a covering role; preserve scope.

Put all parallel agents in one `agents[]` call. Use `depends_on` only for a true prerequisite; otherwise maximize parallelism. This is fire-and-forget: continue useful local work or end the turn for automatic delivery. Do not sleep, predict results, or read `output_file` for progress. If only waiting remains, use `poll(ids=[<returned agent ids>], wait_s=1500, mode='any')`, which returns as soon as an agent finishes; no-id `poll` is a dashboard, not a wait. Each completion arrives with the agent's full result; `get_agent_result` re-reads it later by agent id and swarm_run_id, also after the run ends. If get_agent_result is not visible, discover it with search_tools. A running main agent receives individual results at round boundaries; an idle conversation is auto-resumed only after the whole swarm settles, subject to Stop. Agents launched during such an automatic continuation never wake another one; their results arrive with the next turn. Failures may trigger one bounded diagnosis/closure pass, not an unlimited retry loop. Do not promise a wakeup on each agent completion or treat failed work as side-effect-free.

Novelty and value judgments are provisional and limited to the retrieved evidence. The output is a survey and candidate ideas; research conclusions require reproducible baseline and candidate experiments, independent validation and inspection of originals. Continue the user goal through those stages before claiming empirical gains or publication readiness. Returns immediately with a task_id; the survey runs in the background (several minutes). Use this when the user asks what is worth working on, wants research directions / open problems / a gap analysis in a field — NOT for a written summary of a topic (that is produce_report). Does NOT require an attached project. This is an agent-based tool with an authored workflow: internal models work within fixed stages, with output validation, domain quality checks and durable checkpoints. Call it directly from normal Chat; no Goal mode or free-form agent delegation is needed. A returned task_id confirms acceptance, not delivery. Continue other requested work and let the task panel report progress; do not repeatedly poll or claim a finished artifact from the acceptance receipt.

function.description:
Run builds, tests, lint, installs, Git or pipelines; returns stdout/stderr. NO timeout: runs until it finishes, the user stops it, or you stop a backgrounded one with `kill`. A command still running after 120 s, or when a new message arrives, moves to the background and returns a `bg_*` handle; results arrive automatically. Avoid waiting for stdin.

Fresh subprocess starting in the project root; no persistent shell or environment changes. Start with `cd <dir> && ` to run elsewhere.

Use `read_files`, `search_files`, `find_files`, `edit_file`, `write_file` for repository data. Filesystem grep uses a bounded FUSE-safe engine or returns a `search_files` translation; filtering command output is allowed. `browser_download_url_to_server` handles authenticated browser downloads. Text helpers: `sd`, `mlr`, `goawk`.

An explicit start/end range is authoritative and never widened. Whole-file text reads retain complete sources; model previews are budgeted separately. Batch independent ranges while keeping expected model content near 24k tokens; every requested read executes. Use top-level `path` for one file. Prefer this over shell cat/head/tail/sed. Images are shown natively; PDFs extract layout text; Office files extract Markdown text/tables; text uses encoding detection. Pass exactly one of path or reads. function.name: edit_file

The anchor must match once; replace_all replaces every match. To add text, keep neighbouring text in both: after A: `{"anchor":"A","content":"A\nB"}`; before A: `{"anchor":"A","content":"B\nA"}`. Append at end-of-file with write_file(append=true). Name the file once in `path`; set an edit's `path` only for another file. Later edits see earlier changes. Atomic preflight defaults true: any failure writes nothing. With atomic=false, one failure neither rolls back nor stops the others. I/O failures may leave partial writes. Only explicit project-relative text files are authorized; no aliases, converters, external roots or content refs. Read prefixes: src; write prefixes: src
